title: Per-document signal extraction
description: One file per report at extractions/<doc_id>.json. Written by an LLM agent (Claude Code) from cached page text; every claim carries page-level evidence that verify.py checks in code. No signal may rest on knowledge outside the cited pages.

extracted_by.description: Who/what produced this file. Must name the LLM agent honestly.

report_scope.description: Which industry the report says it covers, so a code mismatch with the chosen NAICS is recorded rather than hidden.

pdf_page.description: 1-based page index in the PDF file (not the printed page label; the printed label is looked up from the cache in code).

section_heading.description: Nearest heading visible on or above the cited page, or null if none is detectable.

quote.description: Verbatim text from the cited page, at most 25 words. Whitespace, case, hyphenation and smart quotes are normalised by the verifier; nothing else may differ.

force_tag.description: S1 context; S2 rivalry; S3 barriers to entry; S4 supplier power; S5 buyer power; S6 and S7 chosen by the extractor, with the reason in value.why_chosen.

value.description: null when NOT_FOUND. Otherwise an object. Every numeric leaf (and every string under a key ending in _range) must appear in an evidence quote of this signal; years and periods are therefore stored as strings, and derived numbers are forbidden.

summary.description: 1-2 sentences in the extractor's own words.

notes.description: Scope caveats: does the figure describe a broader or narrower industry than fractional CFO services? Internal inconsistencies in the source.

S2.competitors: [{name, share_pct: number|null, share_range: string|null, share_basis: string}]

S3.regulation_level: string as stated by the source
